source.title: Sign-Aware Gated Sparse Autoencoders: Modeling Anticorrelated Features with Bi-Jump-ReLU Activations
source.authors: Bartosz Wieciech; Z. Awrahman; M. Czelej; Victor Hugo Jaramillo Velasquez; Wioletta Stobieniecka

record.tranche_reason: The study uses controlled toy geometries and LLM SAE interventions to test related questions about signed feature sharing and feature recovery, but does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.gate_note: Protocol C directly tests consolidation of antipodal feature pairs under increasing superposition. LLM sign-conditioned interventions test whether learned SAE latents have causal effects. The cited Toy Models of Superposition results and the paper’s parameter-counting argument are not experimental result rows. The reconstruction-capacity benchmark is not recorded except where it directly measures the versions above.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE methods paper. It proposes a sign-aware gated SAE (SA-GSAE) and reports that method's own performance. Protocol C trains SAEs on synthetic antipodal feature pairs generated directly in R2, so no network learns a superposed representation. Its consolidation and recoverability metrics measure whether the SAE recovers generating axes, not whether features are stored in superposition. The LLM work measures reconstruction, dead fraction, causal sign-consistency of the method's latents, and a semantic audit of the method and baselines. It assumes the superposition picture as a tool and does not test whether it holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The core conclusion is about the method: a half-width SA-GSAE cuts dead fraction by 0.35–0.82 versus a full-width Gated SAE, matches R2 within 0.025, and frontier-dominates on 3 of 6 cells. The gate and auxiliary loss are essential, and the fully tied variant is recommended. The authors scope interpretability claims to capacity usage and causal bidirectionality, since nameable semantic opposition is rare. They restrict toy pair consolidation to nactive = 1.
record.recipe_differences: The toy validation follows the cited setup’s antipodal-feature framing, but tests a sign-aware SAE and pair-consolidation metrics rather than reproducing the original toy-model method. The LLM studies use SAE training, semantic judgments, and sign-conditioned causal edits.
record.method_sensitivity: Toy pair consolidation changes with nactive and within-pair correlation ρ. LLM causal SCS differs by backbone and hookpoint, with the lowest reported mean at SmolLM3-3B attn.

fits_no_version.finding: A blinded audit finds that the two sides of signed SAE latents, and near-antipodal Gated-SAE pairs, rarely form a nameable semantic opposition. Coherent opposition is 1.5% and unrelated packing about 64%, indistinguishable from random pairings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anticorrelated directions packed onto one SAE axis are mostly statistically, not semantically, paired.

fits_no_version.finding: A single signed SAE latent acts as a bidirectional causal dial (SCS 0.52–0.97). Opposing non-negative Gated-SAE latent pairs do not (pair-SCS −0.38 to −0.71).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Signed dictionary latents capture causally opposed directions that sign-split non-negative latents fail to implement as one axis.

record.problems: The LLM benchmark uses two backbones, three mid-depth hookpoints, and three training seeds. The semantic audit has inter-judge κ = 0.50 and a same-side ceiling judged related in 75% of items. The authors report only aggregate ranges for some intervention controls and toy sweep outcomes; several toy curves are plotted without exact textual values. The study does not establish canonical or complete SAE features.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No toy network learning superposed features, no sparsity-dependent phase transition, no geometry of learned embeddings.
No measurement of features spreading across neurons. SAE recoverability is assumed and used, not tested.
Not tested. The authors explicitly treat SAE dictionaries as non-canonical, citing prior work.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V1/V4 verdicts are overturned. The paper is a T4 method paper that cites Toy Models of Superposition for its antipodal setup. It does not replicate the toy model's learned superposition; data are generated directly in R2 and only the SAE is trained. All rows measure the SAE method or baseline comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test general near-orthogonal geometry for randomly oriented features, a sparsity-dependent transition comparable to the original study, or feature importance.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity arises from feature competition for capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

Tests SAE features and sign-conditioned effects at selected mid-depth sites in two models; does not test feature spreading across neurons or generalize to other model families, layers, or training stages.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional feature subspaces.

rows.subject: Sign-Aware SAE (M = k)
rows.size_stated: M = k; k = 8 for qualitative visualizations and within-pair robustness sweep
rows.operation_detail: Compared learned decoder geometry with ground-truth antipodal feature directions.
rows.baseline: Non-negative baseline at M = 2k learns separate directions for the two features in each pair.
rows.value: The Sign-Aware SAE learns one decoder direction per pair; activation sign distinguishes the two antipodal features.
rows.note: The authors describe the geometry as approximate; exact overlap with generating axes is not expected.
rows.check: Measures SAE decoder geometry on synthetic antipodal data placed directly in R2. No toy network learns superposition, so this is method validation, not V1.

rows.subject: Sign-Aware SAE (M = k)
rows.operation_detail: Measured thresholded Pair Consolidation Rate as the number of simultaneously active feature pairs increased.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SE over 16 seeds is shown in Figure 9; exact uncertainty at nactive ≥ 2 is not stated.
rows.note: The authors state that clean one-latent-per-pair consolidation largely fails at this superposition level, although signed recoverability persists.
rows.check: Pair Consolidation Rate is a metric of the SAE method recovering generating axes. It is not a superposition transition in a learned network.

rows.subject: Sign-Aware SAE (M = k)
rows.operation_detail: Measured signed recoverability under increasing numbers of active feature pairs.
rows.measure: Mean best-candidate activation correlation with the signed ground-truth coefficient
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SE over 16 seeds is shown in Figure 8; exact uncertainty at nactive ≥ 2 is not stated.
rows.note: The paper says signed information persists despite the failure of clean pair consolidation.
rows.check: Signed recoverability of SA-GSAE latents is the method's own performance. It does not bear on V1.

rows.subject: Sign-Aware SAE (M = 2k)
rows.operation_detail: Measured signed recoverability during the superposition sweep.
rows.measure: Signed recoverability across the superposition sweep
rows.value: The overcomplete Sign-Aware setting degrades faster.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SE over 16 seeds is shown in Figure 8; exact values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors describe this as consistent with symmetry between one-latent and two-latent solutions.
rows.check: Compares SA-GSAE widths, i.e. the study's own method across configurations.

rows.subject: Sign-Aware SAE (M = k)
rows.operation_detail: Varied within-pair correlation in the toy feature construction.
rows.value: Consolidation degrades gradually as ρ moves from −1 to 0.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SE over 16 seeds is shown in Figure 10; exact values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors characterize this as a robustness sweep, not a phase transition.
rows.check: Robustness sweep of the method's consolidation rate. The data correlation is set by construction.

rows.subject: Pythia-1B
rows.operation_detail: Applied sign-conditioned, feature-isolated activation edits along sampled SA-GSAE decoder directions.

conditions.value: sampled from the half-width population; 12 held-out active contexts per latent

rows.baseline: Norm-matched random-direction edits have SCS −0.35 to −0.49 across tested cells.
rows.value: Mean SCS 0.97; mean Kendall τ 0.75–0.99 across cells.
rows.note: The report gives the SCS by hookpoint and backbone; this row records the Pythia-1B mlp_out value.
rows.check: Sign-Consistency Score of SA-GSAE latents is the method's causal performance. It does not show models spreading features or the presence of sparse features beyond what any SAE presumes.

rows.subject: Norm-matched random-direction edits
rows.operation_detail: Applied norm-matched positive and negative random-direction edits.
rows.baseline: SA-GSAE sign-conditioned edits have SCS 0.52–0.97 across the six cells.
rows.value: SCS −0.35 to −0.49; both edit directions merely degrade the model in a correlated way.
rows.note: The text reports this control as a range across cells.
rows.check: Random-direction control for the method's intervention metric. Marking it 'reversed' is meaningless relative to any version.

rows.subject: AbsTopK signed latents
rows.operation_detail: Applied sign-conditioned, feature-isolated activation edits along signed latent directions.
rows.value: SCS 0.83–0.99, described as comparable to SA-GSAE.
rows.note: Aggregate range as reported; individual model and hookpoint values are not stated.
rows.check: Baseline-method comparison (AbsTopK), not a result on the claim.

rows.subject: Near-antipodal Gated-SAE latent pairs
rows.operation_detail: Drove the two latents in each pair in opposition and measured the resulting model effects.
rows.baseline: Single signed SA-GSAE latent has pooled SCS 0.83.
rows.value: Pair-SCS −0.38 to −0.71; the pair does not implement one axis according to the authors.
rows.note: The text reports this control as a range across cells.
rows.check: Baseline comparison of Gated-SAE latent pairs under the method's metric. It is not a claim result.

rows.subject: SA-GSAE latents
rows.operation_detail: Blinded audit by two independent frontier-LLM judges of label-free contexts from each latent’s two sides.
rows.note: The authors say the pre-registered hypotheses that SA-GSAE exceeds random controls were not supported (permutation p = 0.70/0.55).
rows.check: Semantic audit of whether the method's two-sided latents encode nameable oppositions. This is a related construct, not any version.

rows.subject: SA-GSAE latents
rows.operation_detail: Blinded audit of whether both sides of a latent were at least partially interpretable to both judges.
rows.measure: Latents with both sides partially interpretable to both judges
rows.note: This measures judged interpretability, not causal recovery; the causal intervention results are recorded separately.
rows.check: Interpretability rate of the method's latents. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: Random cross-latent pairings
rows.operation_detail: Blinded judges classified relations between contexts from randomly paired latents.
rows.note: The audit also reports unrelated packing for random pairings as 65%.
rows.check: Audit control, not a claim result.

rows.subject: SA-GSAE latents
rows.operation_detail: Blinded audit classified the relation between the two sides of each latent.
rows.baseline: Random cross-latent pairings: 65%; AbsTopK signed latents: 59%; near-antipodal Gated-SAE pairs: 63%.
rows.note: The authors report the SA-GSAE rate as statistically indistinguishable from the listed controls.
rows.check: Unrelated-packing rate for the method versus baselines. It is a method-evaluation statistic.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Antipodal toy pairs with ρ = −1 and nactive = 1
reader_labels.reason: A width-k Sign-Aware SAE uses one decoder direction per antipodal pair, with activation sign distinguishing the pair’s two features (r1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Toy superposition sweeps with nactive ≥ 2 and within-pair correlation moving from −1 to 0
reader_labels.reason: Clean one-latent pair consolidation falls below 0.05 at nactive ≥ 2, although signed recoverability remains approximately 0.55 and consolidation degrades gradually as pairs become less anticorrelated (r2–r5).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Sign-conditioned edits of SA-GSAE latents at the tested Pythia-1B and SmolLM3-3B hookpoints
reader_labels.reason: Edits produce positive SCS values of 0.52–0.97, with monotone dose response; random-direction controls do not show the same pattern (r6–r13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Blinded semantic audit of two-sided SA-GSAE latents
reader_labels.reason: Judge-nameable opposition is rare and only 36% of sampled latents had both sides partially interpretable to both judges; unrelated packing is common (r15–r18).
